feedback.summary: You produced an exemplary analysis of Rachel’s dilemma, balancing for/against shipping with a clear decision rule and strong NHS, Therac-25, Intel and VW evidence to justify withholding sign-off. Your stakeholder tables, Figure 1 flowchart, and IEEE sources gave a logical, well-structured argument. You are at Excellent across all criteria – maintain this depth and rigour.
next_steps: Keep using your Figure 1 flowchart and Table 2 options analysis to explicitly link evidence to your recommendations in future reports.
Continue qualifying case limits as you did for the NHS attack versus hardware defect to show balanced judgement.
Sustain your systematic coverage of voiceless stakeholders like patients and later customers alongside commercial interests.

At Excellent top, keep giving depth and stakeholder-specific decision conclusions.

At top Excellent, maintain this compelling linked structure.
criteria.C4: You substantiated arguments with eight reputable sources, quantitative evidence like ‘US$475 million’ Intel charge, Therac deaths, VW 11m/$4.3bn, and qualitative Code duty ‘to communicate honestly and effectively...’, explicitly noting ‘The cause there was an attack...so the case cannot predict...’. At top Excellent, continue combining both evidence types with balanced limits.
criteria.C5: Your ABSTRACT stating ‘This report examines the dilemma of a quality assurance engineer, Rachel’ led into introduction, body, conclusion and RECOMMENDATIONS fluently with Table 1, Figure 1 flowchart and Table 2 competently used and extensive consistent IEEE references including ‘Code of Ethics and Guidelines on Professional Conduct’.
